title: The truncation triangle tau_{<=q-1}K -> tau_{<=q}K -> H^q(K)[-q] is distinguished
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category with derived category $D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], a triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category], with cohomology functors $H^n$ and shift $[1]$, $(M[1])^r=M^{r+1}$, $d_{M[1]}=-d_M$. For a complex $K$ of $\mathcal A$ and $q\in\mathbf Z$ let $\tau_{\leq q}K$ be the canonical truncation, the subcomplex $\cdots\to K^{q-2}\to K^{q-1}\to\Ker(d^q_K)\to0\to\cdots$ of $K$ (the truncation of the standard t-structure [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]), so that $\tau_{\leq q-1}K\subseteq\tau_{\leq q}K$, and let $H^q(K)[-q]$ be the complex with the single object $H^q(K)$ placed in degree $q$. Let $i_q:\tau_{\leq q-1}K\to\tau_{\leq q}K$ be the inclusion and $j_q:\tau_{\leq q}K\to H^q(K)[-q]$ the morphism of complexes which in degree $q$ is the projection $\Ker(d^q_K)\to H^q(K)$ and zero in the other degrees. Then there is a unique morphism $k_q:H^q(K)[-q]\to(\tau_{\leq q-1}K)[1]$ in $D(\mathcal A)$ such that
$$
 \tau_{\leq q-1}K\xrightarrow{\,i_q\,}\tau_{\leq q}K\xrightarrow{\,j_q\,}H^q(K)[-q]\xrightarrow{\,k_q\,}(\tau_{\leq q-1}K)[1]
$$
is a distinguished triangle $T_q(K)$ of $D(\mathcal A)$ (namely $k_q=\delta\circ\bar j_q^{-1}$, where $\delta$ is the boundary morphism of the distinguished triangle of the short exact sequence of complexes $0\to\tau_{\leq q-1}K\to\tau_{\leq q}K\to\tau_{\leq q}K/\tau_{\leq q-1}K\to0$ and $\bar j_q:\tau_{\leq q}K/\tau_{\leq q-1}K\to H^q(K)[-q]$ is the quasi-isomorphism induced by $j_q$). The triangle is functorial in $K$: $\tau_{\leq q}$, $\tau_{\leq q-1}$ and $H^q(-)[-q]$ preserve quasi-isomorphisms and so act on morphisms of $D(\mathcal A)$ [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-descends], and for every morphism $f:K\to L$ of $D(\mathcal A)$ between complexes $K,L$ the triple $(\tau_{\leq q-1}f,\tau_{\leq q}f,H^q(f)[-q])$ is a morphism of triangles $T_q(K)\to T_q(L)$. If $K$ is bounded below (as a complex, or only in cohomology: $H^n(K)=0$ for $n\ll0$), so are the three terms; in particular for $\mathcal A=\Ab(T_{\Et})$ the triangle lies in $\Dplus(T_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories].

source.place: Derived Categories, Remark 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle, line 4076): the canonical distinguished triangle tau_{<=a}K -> tau_{<=a+1}K -> H^{a+1}(K)[-a-1] -> (tau_{<=a}K)[1], from the short exact sequence of truncations and the quasi-isomorphism to H^{a+1}(K)[-a-1]; here a=q-1

proof.text: **Step 1 (the short exact sequence of truncations).** By [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-step-ses] (a), (b), the inclusion $i_q$ sits in a short exact sequence of complexes $0\to\tau_{\leq q-1}K\xrightarrow{i_q}\tau_{\leq q}K\xrightarrow{p_q}M_q(K)\to0$, where $M_q(K)=\tau_{\leq q}K/\tau_{\leq q-1}K$ is the two-term complex $K^{q-1}/\Ker d^{q-1}\to\Ker d^q$ in degrees $q-1,q$ (it is not $H^q(K)[-q]$ itself), and $j_q=\bar j_q\circ p_q$ with $\bar j_q:M_q(K)\to H^q(K)[-q]$ a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Remark 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle, line 4076), second triangle with a=q-1

proof.text: **Step 2 (the triangle of the short exact sequence).** By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] applied to the sequence of Step 1 there is $\delta:M_q(K)\to(\tau_{\leq q-1}K)[1]$ in $D(\mathcal A)$ such that $\tau_{\leq q-1}K\xrightarrow{i_q}\tau_{\leq q}K\xrightarrow{p_q}M_q(K)\xrightarrow{\delta}(\tau_{\leq q-1}K)[1]$ is distinguished.

**Step 3 (existence of $k_q$).** Since $\bar j_q$ is a quasi-isomorphism, its image in the localization $D(\mathcal A)$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $k_q=\delta\circ\bar j_q^{-1}$. Then $(\mathrm{id},\mathrm{id},\bar j_q)$ is an isomorphism from the triangle of Step 2 to $(\tau_{\leq q-1}K,\tau_{\leq q}K,H^q(K)[-q],i_q,j_q,k_q)$: the squares read $i_q\circ\mathrm{id}=\mathrm{id}\circ i_q$, $\bar j_q\circ p_q=j_q\circ\mathrm{id}$ (Step 1) and $k_q\circ\bar j_q=\delta=\mathrm{id}[1]\circ\delta$. A triangle isomorphic to a distinguished triangle is distinguished (TR1 of [def-weil-triangulated-category]), so $T_q(K)$ is distinguished.

source.place: Remark 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle, line 4076), second triangle with a=q-1

proof.text: **Step 4 (a vanishing of morphisms).** For complexes $K,L$: $\Hom_{D(\mathcal A)}\bigl((\tau_{\leq q-1}K)[1],H^q(L)[-q]\bigr)=0$. Indeed $\tau_{\leq q-1}K$ is a complex with zero terms in degrees $>q-1$, so $(\tau_{\leq q-1}K)[1]$ has zero terms in degrees $>q-2$ and lies in $D(\mathcal A)^{\leq q-2}$; $H^q(L)[-q]$ has zero terms in degrees $<q$ and lies in $D(\mathcal A)^{\geq q}\subseteq D(\mathcal A)^{\geq q-1}$ [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. By axiom 2 of a t-structure, shifted by $q-2$ ($\Hom(A,B[-1])=0$ for $A\in D^{\leq0}$, $B\in D^{\geq0}$, i.e. $\Hom(D^{\leq n},D^{\geq n+1})=0$) [def-weil-t-structure], every morphism between them is zero.

source.place: Définition 1.3.1 (i) and Exemple 1.3.2 (i) (the natural t-structure on D(A): complexes quasi-isomorphic to complexes zero in degrees > n, resp. < n), pdf page 30

proof.text: **Step 5 (uniqueness of $k_q$).** Let $k'_q$ be another morphism making $(\tau_{\leq q-1}K,\tau_{\leq q}K,H^q(K)[-q],i_q,j_q,k'_q)$ distinguished. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-triangle-morphism-extension] (2) to the triangles $T=(\ldots,k_q)$, $T'=(\ldots,k'_q)$, $g=\mathrm{id}_{\tau_{\leq q}K}$, $f=\mathrm{id}$, $h=\mathrm{id}$: the squares $i_q\circ\mathrm{id}=\mathrm{id}\circ i_q$ and $\mathrm{id}\circ j_q=j_q\circ\mathrm{id}$ commute and $\Hom((\tau_{\leq q-1}K)[1],H^q(K)[-q])=0$ by Step 4, so $(\mathrm{id},\mathrm{id},\mathrm{id})$ is a morphism of triangles, i.e. $k'_q=k_q$ (this is BBD 1.1.10 (ii), part (3) of the lemma). So the 'unique' of the statement holds: although in general the third arrow completing two given arrows to a distinguished triangle is not unique, here $\Hom(X[1],Z)=0$ for the first and third terms.

**Step 6 (functoriality).** Let $f:K\to L$ be a morphism of $D(\mathcal A)$ between complexes. By [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-descends] there are morphisms $a=\tau_{\leq q-1}f$, $b=\tau_{\leq q}f$, $c=H^q(f)[-q]$ in $D(\mathcal A)$ with $b\circ i_q=i_q\circ a$ and $c\circ j_q=j_q\circ b$ (naturality of $i_q$, $j_q$ on $D(\mathcal A)$). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-triangle-morphism-extension] (2) to the distinguished triangles $T_q(K)$, $T_q(L)$ (Step 3) and $g=b$: since $\Hom((\tau_{\leq q-1}K)[1],H^q(L)[-q])=0$ (Step 4), $(a,b,c)$ is a morphism of triangles, i.e. also $k_q(L)\circ c=a[1]\circ k_q(K)$. (For $f=Q(\phi)$ a morphism of complexes this is also the image of the morphism of short exact sequences of [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-step-ses] (c) under the naturality of [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle].)

**Step 7 (bounded below).** If $K$ is a bounded below complex, so are its subcomplexes $\tau_{\leq q}K$, $\tau_{\leq q-1}K$, and $H^q(K)[-q]$ has one nonzero term. If only $H^n(K)=0$ for $n<n_0$: $H^n(\tau_{\leq q}K)=H^n(K)$ for $n\leq q$ and $=0$ for $n>q$ (the cohomology of the canonical truncation, read off degreewise: in degree $q$, $\Ker d^q/\Im d^{q-1}$), likewise for $q-1$, and $H^n(H^q(K)[-q])$ is $H^q(K)$ for $n=q$ and $0$ otherwise; so all three have $H^n=0$ for $n<\min(n_0,q)$ and lie in $D^+$; for $\mathcal A=\Ab(T_{\Et})$ this is $\Dplus(T_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories].

source.place: Section 0118 (section-truncations, line 3612), the cohomology of the canonical truncations

split_report.summary: Split along Stacks Remark 08J5 into: the short exact sequence of complexes 0 -> tau_{<=q-1}K -> tau_{<=q}K -> M_q(K) -> 0 with M_q(K) the two-term complex K^{q-1}/Ker d^{q-1} -> Ker d^q (not H^q(K)[-q] itself) and the quasi-isomorphism M_q(K) -> H^q(K)[-q] (new lem-weil-pbc-truncation-step-ses, unsplit); the distinguished triangle of a short exact sequence of complexes, functorial (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle, DerivedCategory.triangleOfSES_distinguished; the existing leaf lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle only covers single objects in degree 0 and does not apply); existence of k_q by transport along the quasi-isomorphism (TR1). Checked uniqueness: it holds, because Hom((tau_{<=q-1}K)[1], H^q(K)[-q]) = 0 (D^{<=q-2} against D^{>=q}, step 4 from the standard t-structure); proved via BBD Prop. 1.1.9 / Cor. 1.1.10 (ii) (new lem-weil-pbc-triangle-morphism-extension, unsplit), which also gives the third square of functoriality. Functoriality in D(A) needs the truncation functors on D(A) (new lem-weil-pbc-truncation-descends, unsplit; added to stmt_deps since the statement uses tau_{<=q}f for f in D(A)). Statement kept, with def-weil-triangulated-category and lem-weil-pbc-truncation-descends added to stmt_deps, the functoriality clause made precise and the bounded-below clause extended to cohomologically bounded below K. Not a Mathlib leaf: Mathlib has the t-structure triangle with third term tau_{>=q}tau_{<=q}K and no identification with the single complex H^q(K)[-q].
